evidence_scope.statement: BrainOS received, over Lab Streaming Layer, exactly the data the reference software recorded from the same source, within the stated tolerances. This is software-level evidence about the acquisition path; it says nothing about hardware unless the source was real hardware and the hardware criteria below are met.
not_a_hardware_run_because: the operator did not declare acquisition hardware as the signal source
overlap 10 s < 240 s required for a hardware-validation run
evidence_scope.note: brainos-hwval never sets hardware_verified or human_validated (docs/VALIDATION_LEVELS.md, docs/HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md).

acquisition.reference_software: XDF file (LabRecorder or compatible), read with pyxdf

checks.title: Reference XDF stream is readable and consistent
checks.summary: 13870 samples read by pyxdf (footer sample_count 13869 vs 13870 samples read (LabRecorder footer count; the samples themselves are authoritative))
checks.method: pyxdf loads the file (synchronize_clocks=False, dejitter_timestamps=False); sample and timestamp counts must agree.

notes: footer sample_count 13869 vs 13870 samples read (LabRecorder footer count; the samples themselves are authoritative)

checks.title: BrainOS recording file is complete and well-formed
checks.summary: 494 frames, every line readable, seq contiguous, contract-valid
checks.method: Parse every line; require the brainos.recording/1 header, contiguous envelope seq numbers (the recorder writes every published event), and — if BrainOS is installed — validation of every envelope against BrainOS's contract models.

checks.title: Both recordings are of the same LSL stream
checks.summary: same LSL outlet (uid f6b65d83-d7e5-417f-8adb-2565d7e60348)
checks.method: XDF stream chosen by the capture sidecar's uid, else the stream name/source_id/host in the BrainOS device descriptor, else a unique channel count + rate; then every identity field available on both sides must agree.

checks.title: Channel count and channel identities agree
checks.summary: 8 channels, labels identical in order
checks.method: Channel count of every BrainOS frame and of the descriptor equals the XDF channel_count; the descriptor's channel_labels equal the XDF <channel><label> list in order (BrainOS names an unlabelled channel 'ch<i>').

checks.title: Declared sampling rate agrees
checks.summary: 1000 Hz on both sides
checks.method: sample_rate_hz of every BrainOS frame and of the descriptor equals the XDF nominal_srate.

checks.title: Stream type and sample format agree
checks.summary: EEG / float32
checks.method: Descriptor stream_type and channel_format equal the XDF type and channel_format.

checks.title: Units are interpreted correctly
checks.summary: reference declares voltage units; BrainOS reports µV
checks.method: If every XDF channel declares a known voltage unit (microvolts, millivolts, volts, nanovolts and abbreviations), BrainOS must label frames 'uV' (values converted); otherwise it must label them 'arbitrary' (values unscaled).

checks.title: Synthetic / prerecorded declarations are carried through
checks.summary: declarations consistent (the data is declared synthetic)
checks.method: The publisher's optional <desc><brainos><synthetic>/<prerecorded> declarations must appear as provenance synthetic / replayed on every BrainOS frame, and BrainOS must not add them on its own.

checks.title: Recordings overlap enough to compare
checks.summary: 10.49 s of the recordings overlap (10490 samples)
checks.method: Span from the first to the last reference sample that a BrainOS frame maps to. BrainOS samples before the reference started or after it stopped are not compared and not counted as errors.

checks.title: Sample counts agree within the overlap
checks.summary: reference 10490 vs BrainOS 10490 samples in the overlap
checks.method: Count reference samples between the first and last BrainOS sample and the BrainOS samples mapped onto them (each counted once per frame that claims it).

checks.title: No samples missing in BrainOS
checks.summary: no reference sample is missing from BrainOS
checks.method: Reference samples inside the overlap that no BrainOS frame maps to.

checks.title: No duplicated samples in BrainOS
checks.summary: none
checks.method: Reference samples claimed by more than one BrainOS frame.

checks.title: No BrainOS samples without a reference counterpart
checks.summary: every BrainOS sample in the reference's range has a counterpart
checks.method: BrainOS frames whose first-sample key lies within the reference's range but matches no reference sample.

checks.title: BrainOS frames are in source order
checks.summary: frames in source order
checks.method: Successive frames (in recording order) must map to increasing reference rows; a frame that cannot be mapped must not have a smaller first_sample_index than its predecessor.

checks.title: Alignment confirmed by signal content (independent of timestamps)
checks.summary: 24 probed frame(s) found by content exactly where their timestamps/indices place them
checks.method: For evenly spaced frames (and every frame the key could not place), search the reference values for the frame's first 16 samples on all channels; compare the row found with the row given by the frame's timestamp / sample number.

checks.title: Signal values agree within the expected numerical tolerance
checks.summary: all 83920 values agree (83920 bit-exact)
checks.method: Every BrainOS sample is compared with the reference sample it maps to, channel by channel: |brainos - reference| <= tolerance. |diff| <= 0 + 2.5e-07 x |reference| (reference converted to BrainOS's unit in float64). Bit-exact values are counted separately ('exact'); a difference at single-precision level is an expected numerical tolerance.

evidence.tolerance: |diff| <= 0 + 2.5e-07 x |reference| (reference converted to BrainOS's unit in float64). Bit-exact values are counted separately ('exact'); a difference at single-precision level is an expected numerical tolerance.

checks.title: Channels are in the reference order
checks.summary: every channel matches its reference channel
checks.method: Every BrainOS channel is matched against every reference channel on a thin sample.

checks.title: Scaling and units are correct
checks.summary: values equal the reference in the stated unit (factor 1)
checks.method: Least-squares factor per channel on a thin sample.

checks.title: BrainOS reported every loss it suffered
checks.summary: no loss to report (1 frame(s) flagged anyway)
checks.method: For each run of samples missing in BrainOS, the next BrainOS frame must carry the quality flag dropped_samples, or a device.status event (reconnecting, ...) must lie between the frames around the gap.

checks.title: Timestamps agree with the reference
checks.summary: first-sample timestamps of 494 frames equal the source timestamps (max |diff| 4.5e-13 s)
checks.method: Each BrainOS frame's device_timestamp_ns (source clock) is compared with the XDF raw timestamp of the sample it maps to; both are copies of the source's timestamps, so any difference above 2e-06 s is an error. Frames located by content at another sample are timestamp errors.

checks.title: Data was not delayed beyond the threshold
checks.summary: worst excess ingest delay 9.8 ms (median 2.7 ms) vs threshold 1000 ms; absolute latency median 4.4 ms
checks.method: BrainOS ingest wall clock minus the source time of each frame's last sample; the excess over the smallest observed value is the variable delay (buffering, transport, stalls). Absolute latency uses the clock pair measured by `brainos-hwval capture`.

checks.title: Effective sampling rate matches the nominal rate
checks.summary: effective rate 1000.0000 Hz (+0.0 ppm from nominal)
checks.method: Linear fit of the reference's raw timestamps against sample number over the longest gap-free segment; the same fit over BrainOS frame timestamps vs first_sample_index. Advisory: this measures the source, not BrainOS.

checks.title: Reference stream is continuous
checks.summary: the reference itself has 1 gap(s) (~150 samples) and 0 timestamp regression(s): source or recorder discontinuities
checks.method: Per-sample XDF timestamps: an interval > 1.5 periods (and > 2 ms beyond one period) is a gap; a non-increasing timestamp is a regression. Advisory: a discontinuity here is in the source or in LabRecorder, not in BrainOS.

checks.title: Clock offset and drift characterised
checks.summary: recorder-source offset median -0.019 ms, drift +1.54 ppm; BrainOS wall clock vs source drift +8.34 ppm
checks.method: Linear fit of LabRecorder's ClockOffset chunks (recorder minus source clock) against time; separately, BrainOS ingest wall clock minus source time against source time. Advisory: these characterise the clocks involved; offsets between clock domains are expected and are not errors.

checks.title: Acquisition hardware and software are documented
checks.summary: no equipment manifest given (--equipment); the run is not traceable to hardware
checks.method: Required fields of the brainos-hwval.equipment/1 manifest must be filled in.

limitations: Both recordings receive the stream through liblsl. A defect that liblsl itself introduced before either inlet (e.g. in the outlet's buffer) would be invisible to this comparison; comparing against the acquisition device's own file format closes that gap.

BrainOS stores one source timestamp per frame (its first sample); per-sample timestamps inside a frame are reconstructed as first + k / nominal rate. The reconstruction error is reported but BrainOS cannot be checked for per-sample timestamp fidelity.
LSL carries no sequence numbers: a sample lost before both inlets (at the source) appears as the same gap in both recordings and is reported as a source discontinuity, not as BrainOS loss.
Absolute ingest latency needs the clock pair measured by `brainos-hwval capture`; otherwise only delay variation (excess over the best case) and drift are measured.
A software publisher or a file player is not hardware. LSL cannot tell hardware from playback; the source kind is what the operator declares in the equipment manifest.
